sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, 14.2 Self-Inductance and Inductors
sources.readSections: 14.6–14.14: flux linkage, sign convention, self emf, steady current and long-solenoid construction
sources.shortQuote: If the current is not changing over time, the flux is not changing in time, so no emf is induced.
sources.support: For linear fixed L, linkage NΦ=LI and source emf ε=−L dI/dt. For a long solenoid with fixed geometry the turn count enters linkage twice, giving N². These are physical relations taught in this goal, not a demand to solve an ODE.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, 14.4 RL Circuits
sources.shortQuote: The smaller the inductive time constant
sources.support: A constant-source, series-RL circuit from I(0)=0 satisfies U−L dI/dt−RI=0, I(t)=(U/R)(1−exp(−Rt/L)) and τ=L/R. This constrains a delay comparison to the stated whole circuit and initial condition; it is distinct from imposing equal I(t).

sources.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, University of Texas at Austin, Self Inductance
sources.readSections: Entire bounded page: equations 2.322–2.330 and physical/circuit assumptions
sources.shortQuote: The inductance and resistance of the solenoid are represented by a perfect inductor
sources.support: Equations distinguish generated back emf from passive voltage drop and model coil resistance separately in series; time constant L/R and initial condition are explicit. This source uses N for turns per length, unlike our N for total turns; notation is translated, not copied.

ownInference: At identical prescribed dI/dt, differing L gives differing emf, with no new current-delay inference. At equal fixed source U, equal total R and zero initial currents, larger L yields slower buildup. Equal emf alone never identifies the circuit ratio L/R. Core μ scaling is already explicit in the unchanged whole current physics predecessor 106417ed; together with λ=NΦ it gives the qualitative linear-core comparison.
